title: Depth over Fidelity in Fixed-Budget Noisy Evolution Strategies
claim: Preserving optimizer depth while handling noise via selection-stage uncertainty beats spending the budget on per-candidate denoising, giving lower final regret.
layout: 2x2 grid of log-log convergence plots, each with a depth colorbar on the right
description: Four convergence plots in a 2x2 grid, titled bbob-noisy f10, f13, f16 and f25. A shared legend at the top lists five methods: CMA-ES, Resample (k=5), Resample (k=10), UH-CMA-ES and Residual Bootstrapping. The x-axis is function evaluations on a log scale and the y-axis is regret f(x_best) minus f*, also on a log scale. Each method is a solid median line with a shaded interquartile band. The blue Residual Bootstrapping curve falls below the others in the later part of each run. The Resample and UH-CMA-ES curves stay higher. Next to each plot is a vertical gradient colorbar labeled 'Depth (generations)', running from 0 to 250. Colored dots on it mark how many generations each method completed. The blue and red dots sit near the bottom (deep), and the purple, olive and orange dots sit near the top (shallow). Steep spikes at the right edge of each plot are rendering artifacts.
caption: RB-PEM improves fixed-budget progress on COCO bbob-noisy. Median (solid) and interquartile range (shaded) of log10(f(ˆx) −f ⋆) versus evaluations on four representative high-misranking functions (f110, f113, f116, f125; d = 40, B = 100d, 15 instances each). Right-side markers indicate the number of completed CMA-ES generations (depth). Methods that preserve depth (CMA-ES, RB-PEM) generally achieve lower final regret; among these, RB-PEM further improves by integrating ranking uncertainty at the selection stage rather than spending evaluations on per-candidate denoising. Evaluation-stage baselines (Resample, UH-CMA-ES) sacrifice depth for per-generation fidelity, resulting in higher final regret despite cleaner intra-generation rankings. Protocol: Each of the 15 COCO instances is run once per method (no repeated seeds); lines show the median and shading spans the 25th–75th percentile (IQR) across instances.
abstract: Noisy evolution strategies under fixed evaluation budgets face a depth-fidelity trade-off: spending evaluations to denoise intra-generation rankings reduces the number of distribution updates the optimizer can execute. We argue for depth over fidelity and propose probabilistic elite membership (PEM), which replaces hard rank-based weights in evolution strategies with conditional expected rank weights that integrate over ranking uncertainty. PEM preserves the conditional mean update while reducing conditional update dispersion, a Rao-Blackwellization of the noisy rank-based step. We instantiate PEM via residual bootstrapping (RB-PEM) with capped per-generation overhead, complemented by an adaptive probe-and-switch mechanism for low-noise regimes. Across the COCO bbob-noisy suite and external tasks including RL policy search and hyperparameter optimization, RB-PEM achieves consistent gains in high-misranking, budget-constrained settings.
